system_description.narrative_title: Middle East conflict-driven oil shock and market ripple effects
system_description.narrative_summary: Escalating U.S.-Iran tensions, attacks on Gulf infrastructure and shadow shipping operations are producing a sustained oil-price shock that reverberates through commodity, financial and real-economy channels. Described as an open system, physical flows (oil shipments, storage), state actions (military strikes, diplomacy, sanctions), market signals (prices, risk premia) and policy responses (stockpiling, insurance, central-bank expectations) interact with feedbacks and time lags so that partial recovery of flows can coexist with elevated volatility and persistent inflationary pressure. The narrative links concrete events (attacks, tanker incidents, policy statements) to systemic variables (supply risk, shipping bottlenecks, risk premia, inflation expectations) that propagate across adjacent sectors.
system_description.scope: Persian Gulf oil production and export flows; tanker/shipping routes (including 'shadow' fleets) and storage/stockpiles; regional state actions and proxy attacks (Iran, Saudi Arabia, UAE, Houthi, U.S., Turkey, others); immediate market outcomes across oil, gas, metals and equity markets; short-term transport and consumer impacts (airfares, fuel shortages).
system_description.super_system: Global energy-financial-geopolitical system (global economy, commodity markets and international security order)
adjacent_subsystems: Global maritime shipping, insurance and logistics
Global financial and commodity trading markets (oil, metals, FX, derivatives)
Regional Middle East political-military networks and diplomacy

variables.name: Oil export flow rate
variables.description: Volume of crude and refined oil leaving the producing region per unit time along export routes.

variables.name: Upstream capacity utilization
variables.description: Proportion of available upstream production capacity that is operating and supplying the market.

variables.name: Shipping bottleneck index
variables.description: Aggregate degree of delay, route congestion and port/terminal throughput constraint affecting maritime transport.

variables.name: Tanker freight rate level
variables.description: Price level charged for maritime transport of oil (dry and liquid cargo freight rates averaged across routes).

variables.name: Maritime insurance premium
variables.description: Average cost of war-risk and hull/cargo insurance for vessels operating in the affected sea lanes.

variables.name: Oil price level
variables.description: Market price of benchmark crude oil expressed as an aggregated spot/futures price level.

variables.name: Oil price volatility
variables.description: Magnitude and frequency of oil-price fluctuations measured over short-to-medium horizons.

variables.name: Supply disruption risk
variables.description: Market-perceived likelihood and expected severity of interruptions to oil production or export flows.

variables.name: Strategic reserve volume
variables.description: Quantity of oil held in designated strategic/state reserves available for release.

variables.name: Commercial storage level
variables.description: Total inventory of oil and refined products held in commercial tanks and floating storage.

variables.name: Shadow fleet utilization
variables.description: Degree to which nontransparent or reflagged shipping capacity is being used to move oil outside standard channels.

variables.name: Maritime security incident rate
variables.description: Frequency of hostile actions, attacks, seizures or sabotage affecting vessels and offshore infrastructure.

variables.name: Sanctions enforcement intensity
variables.description: Degree and rigor with which trade-restricting measures and interdictions are applied and enforced on oil flows.

variables.name: Inflation expectations
variables.description: Average market and agent expectations for future consumer price inflation over policy-relevant horizons.

variables.name: Monetary policy expectations
variables.description: Market consensus on future central-bank policy rates and the trajectory of monetary tightening or easing.

variables.name: Financial spillover strength
variables.description: Degree to which commodity-price and shipping shocks transmit to equities, bonds, precious metals and FX markets.

catalysts.title: Possible U.S. strikes on Iran
catalysts.description: Threatened or limited U.S. military operations against Iran that could occur in the coming weeks, prompting immediate security and market reaction.
catalysts.rationale: "Trump says US may do another military operation against Iran"; markets price fresh U.S.-Iran strike risk.

catalysts.title: Continued maritime/energy attacks (Houthis/Saudi)
catalysts.description: Ongoing Houthi and related strikes on Saudi and shipping targets that sustain elevated risks to sea lanes and infrastructure.
catalysts.rationale: "Fresh attacks in Saudi Arabia show risks remain"; reports of Houthi attacks and supply concerns.

catalysts.title: Diplomatic push to head off escalation
catalysts.description: Intense diplomatic activity aimed at preventing U.S.-Iran escalation; could reduce military risk if successful.
catalysts.rationale: "Diplomats Race to Head Off Escalation With Iran"; markets moving on hopes for de‑escalation.

catalysts.title: U.S. 2026 midterm elections
catalysts.description: U.S. midterm vote that could influence administration risk tolerance and foreign-policy decisions related to the Iran conflict.
catalysts.rationale: Headline links market nerves to "midterm elections near" influencing predicted U.S. strikes and policy.

catalysts.title: Aramco seeks partners to expand stockpile
catalysts.description: Saudi Aramco's effort to partner with other countries to expand oil stockpiles, potentially enlarging strategic/commercial buffers.
catalysts.rationale: "Saudi Aramco seeks to partner with countries to expand its oil stockpile," implying reserve builds.

catalysts.title: Intensified sanctions/interdictions on Iranian trade
catalysts.description: Continued U.S. pressure, interdictions and enforcement that shrink Iran's overland and covert export channels.
catalysts.rationale: "Iran’s Fleet of Shadow Tankers Has Run Out of Oil" and "Iran Is Now Losing Overland Trade Routes to U.S. Pressure."

catalysts.title: Protracted U.S.–Iran stalemate
catalysts.description: A durable, low-intensity stand‑off rather than decisive resolution, maintaining elevated risk premia in markets.
catalysts.rationale: "US prepared for protracted stalemate with Iran" — implies sustained market risk premia and spillovers.
